newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian CPI around 2.7 pct yr/yr in Nov - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italian CPI around 2.7 pct yr/yr in Nov - Ciampi.

text.p: Italian inflation should fall to around 2.7 percent year-on-year in November and will then hold close to that level for sometime, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in a newspaper interview.
Annual inflation in October was 3.0 percent.

"In a few days time we will have inflation data for November at around 2.7 percent. For a while we will halt there and the subsequent fall will not be speedy," Ciampi was quoted as telling L'Unita newspaper.
The government has forecast an annual inflation rate of 2.5 percent for 1997.
"To get to the 2.5 percent target...it will be enough to reach the end of (next) year with an inflation level of 2.3 percent," Ciampi said.

"We are currently in a virtuous circle. However everything could fall apart. We're on a knife's edge. This is our risk. The virtuous circle is running but it is a delicate mechanism and won't take any knocks," he added. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
